Left: with induced=False extra edges are allowed, so the path maps onto B–A and B–C (in the accent color) and is_subgraph_isomorphic(p, induced=False) returns True. Right: with the default induced=True the matched nodes may have no extra edge, but the edge A–C (in the accent color) closes every candidate path into the triangle, so is_subgraph_isomorphic(p) returns False." width="100%"} A pattern occurs when its nodes can be matched to distinct nodes of this graph so that every pattern edge corresponds to an edge here. With `induced=True` (the default), the matched nodes must also have no *extra* edges among them, so the pattern appears as an induced subgraph: a path of three nodes then does not occur inside a triangle. With `induced=False`, extra edges are allowed (a *monomorphism*), so any pattern whose edges can be found is reported. Searching for small patterns is how motifs, functional groups in molecules, fraud patterns in transaction graphs, or forbidden structures in a design are found. Both graphs must have the same directedness. Parallel edges and self-loops in the pattern must be matched by the same number of edges (`induced=True`) or at least as many (`induced=False`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The `Graph` to search for. It is not modified. [induced]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), require an induced subgraph; if `False`, allow extra edges. [node_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node attribute name, or list of names, whose values must be equal for matched nodes. [edge_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | list[str] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional edge attribute name, or list of names, whose values must be equal for matched edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if at least one occurrence exists. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If one graph is directed and the other is not. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The search is the VF2++ style backtracking used by `is_isomorphic()`, mapping the pattern into this graph and stopping at the first occurrence. Subgraph isomorphism is NP-complete in general, but small patterns are found quickly. NetworkX's `GraphMatcher(G, pattern).subgraph_is_isomorphic()` and `subgraph_is_monomorphic()` answer the same questions. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A triangle contains a path of three nodes as a subgraph, but not as an *induced* subgraph, since the third edge of the triangle closes the path: ::: {#ca187af3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec triangle = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(3) path = ec.Graph().add_path_graph(3) triangle.is_subgraph_isomorphic(path), triangle.is_subgraph_isomorphic(path, induced=False) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (False, True) ``` ::: ::: A square does contain the path as an induced subgraph: ::: {#6400514e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(4).is_subgraph_isomorphic(path) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
